$comment: The index's curated data. catalog is a snapshot of the library catalogue, written by build-index.mjs --catalog <file> --write: never edit it by hand. Edit categoryNotes, rowRules, tasks, requireManifests, buildOrders (with their copies, installs, generates and noManifest), verifyGreen and closure here, then run build-index.mjs --write and check-index.mjs.

categoryNotes.start-here: The front door: which skills a task needs and in which order.
categoryNotes.process: How every change is made, whatever it touches: test-first, gated, traced, committed and reported.
categoryNotes.setup: The repo itself: the skeleton, the layout and its boundaries, the code rules, packages, SDK upgrades, native generation and variants.
categoryNotes.ui: What the user sees and touches: components, screens, states, forms, layout, motion, sound, icons, canvases and the proof that a screen matches its design.
categoryNotes.navigation: Routes and links, the cold start, and the settings that change how the app behaves.
categoryNotes.data: State, server data, sign-in, the database and its migrations, backups, typed errors, async safety, dates, money and seeded content.
categoryNotes.i18n-a11y-perf: Text in every language, right-to-left layouts, accessibility and performance budgets.
categoryNotes.platform: Device features behind ports: notifications, permissions, media, background work, native modules and the opt-in web target.
categoryNotes.money-privacy: Ads, purchases, privacy declarations, crash reporting and analytics, each gated on consent where the stores require it.
categoryNotes.testing: Unit, component, golden and end-to-end tests, and the test-only hooks that make devices scriptable.
categoryNotes.release: Builds on simulators and emulators, EAS, the App Store and Google Play, over-the-air updates and CI.
categoryNotes.games: Optional: pure rules engines, levels and solvers, the game host, balance bots and real-time loops.

rowRules.why: every screen, component, state or form change - whoever leads the task - is checked in both themes, LTR and RTL, at the largest text size, against its approved design, on iOS and Android
product code changes start with a failing test; the tests and the report are the review
a store build or update ships only with current privacy answers and a tagged, evidenced report

buildOrders.title: A new app from an empty repo
buildOrders.intro: One Expo app at the repo root (src/ layout, the @/ alias, Expo Router), iOS and Android from day one. The skeleton holds only what its own configs and gates need, so every gate is green on day one; each later step adds the layer the next one depends on. Each skill's checker reports its part as missing until its step: that is the order, not a bug. When the repo is a monorepo, each skill's "When multi-package" section applies.

buildOrders.title: A release to the App Store and Google Play
buildOrders.intro: From a green main branch to builds in TestFlight and a Play testing track, on EAS Build and Submit (eas-build-and-submit owns the store sequence). Every check that reads configuration baked into the binary (variants, eas.json profiles, the update channel and runtime version, the crash reporter's source-map upload) runs at step 4, before anything is built, so a FAIL never costs a build number. A team without EAS takes the local lanes instead: `npm run release:ios` (ios-release-testflight) and the local Play upload (android-release-play), each behind the same artifact gates; the steps that carry a local-lane proof say what it runs instead (step 4 runs `check-eas-config.mjs .` without --release, which prints NOT APPLICABLE or the internal-only EAS note), and those skills' local-lane commands replace steps 5 to 8. Ship gates never skip: their only relaxation is a keyless --rehearsal, which is never release evidence. Stop and ask the developer before the store build, every submission, every tag push and every rollout change.

steps.step: Verify the tree and the gates
steps.proof: `npm run verify` is green; `check-bypasses.mjs .` (quality-gates) and `check-tests.mjs .` (tdd-workflow) print RESULT: PASS

steps.step: The design review: every screen, theme, direction, text size and device class, signed off
Privacy: SDK inventory, the iOS privacy manifest, App Privacy and Data safety answers
Build configuration in ship mode, before any build: variants, eas.json profiles, remote build numbers, submit ids, the update channel and fingerprint runtime, crash-report source maps
steps.proof: `check-eas-config.mjs . --release` (eas-build-and-submit), `check-variants.mjs .` (app-variants-and-environment), `check-ota.mjs .` (ota-updates) and `check-crash-reporting.mjs .` (crash-reporting-and-observability) print RESULT: PASS (the last two may print NOT APPLICABLE when the app ships no updates or no crash reporter)
steps.localLane: `check-eas-config.mjs .` (eas-build-and-submit) without --release prints NOT APPLICABLE or the internal-only EAS note; `check-variants.mjs .` (app-variants-and-environment), `check-ota.mjs .` (ota-updates), `check-crash-reporting.mjs .` (crash-reporting-and-observability), `check-release-setup.mjs .` (ios-release-testflight) and `check-play-release-setup.mjs . --release` (android-release-play) print RESULT: PASS (or NOT APPLICABLE for updates and crash reporting)

steps.step: The preflight: `node scripts/eas/release-preflight.ts --profile production --platform all --what-to-test "<text>"` runs verify, checks the tree, the profile and the version, writes the fingerprints to dist/eas/ and prints the release sequence; then stop and ask the developer for the store build (one message: version, platforms, what will be uploaded)
steps.proof: The preflight exits 0 and the developer said yes to the store build in this session; nothing was built before that

steps.step: The store build and its record: `eas build --profile production --platform all --non-interactive --freeze-credentials --message '<commit subject>' --json > dist/eas/builds.json` (never --auto-submit for Android, never --latest later)
steps.proof: `check-eas-build.mjs . --build dist/eas/builds.json --platform ios` and `check-eas-build.mjs . --build dist/eas/builds.json --platform android` (eas-build-and-submit) print RESULT: PASS: finished store builds of the production profile, from the reviewed commit, with a build number above every upload tag and the preflight's fingerprint

steps.step: iOS: download the record's .ipa to build/ios-release/export/app.ipa, gate it, then after the developer says yes `eas submit --profile production --platform ios --path build/ios-release/export/app.ipa --non-interactive --what-to-test '<text>'`
steps.proof: `check-store-artifact.mjs . --ipa build/ios-release/export/app.ipa --variant production --version <x.y.z> --build <n>` (ios-release-testflight) prints RESULT: PASS before the submit; the submission reaches VALID processing in App Store Connect

steps.step: Android: download the record's bundle to build/release-android/app-release.aab, gate it, then after the developer says yes `eas submit --profile production --platform android --path build/release-android/app-release.aab --non-interactive` to the testing track
steps.proof: `check-play-release-setup.mjs . --release` and `check-store-aab.mjs . --aab build/release-android/app-release.aab --version-code <n> --stamp build/release-android/aab-gate.json` (android-release-play) print RESULT: PASS before the submit

steps.step: After the builds: confirm each build record's channel and runtime version match what step 4 checked, and that this build's source maps and debug symbols reached the crash reporter (nothing here changes a shipped binary)
steps.proof: The build records in dist/eas/builds.json name the production channel and the preflight's runtime version, and the crash reporter lists this release with its source maps; `check-ota.mjs .` (ota-updates) and `check-crash-reporting.mjs .` (crash-reporting-and-observability) still print RESULT: PASS or NOT APPLICABLE
steps.localLane: The archive's and the bundle's channel and runtime version come from the same app config step 4 checked; confirm the crash reporter lists this release with its source maps and debug symbols

steps.step: Tag each submitted build from its record (v<x.y.z>+ios.<n>, v<x.y.z>+android.<n>), push the tags only with the developer's word, and report the release

verifyGreen.intro: `npm run verify` (quality-gates' runner) runs its steps in order and stops at the first red one. On an app built in this order a gate is expected red only before its "Green from" step, for the reason given, and that is not a failure of the step in progress: run the other gates one by one meanwhile and name the pending gate in the report. Any other red gate is a real failure of the step that turned it red. test:sim joins verify only when the first *.sim.test.ts exists (games plugin), and a gate another skill appends to quality-gates.json "verifyExtraSteps" is green from the step that adds it.
